review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its small API lemmas against Mathlib's Scheme.Modules Sheaf.lean and Category/Preorder.lean. I also grepped the repository for uses of the local lemmas. I did not run Lean, so the replacements below are untested. The file has no @[simp] declarations of its own. The findings therefore concern missing or redundant simp-level coverage and the reversed-direction `simp only` chain. I did not examine the effect of the large `attribute [-simp]` list at the top. The first finding is moderate and the other two are minor.

findings.excerpt: theorem zero_app_apply {M N : X.Modules} (U : X.Opens) (m : Γ(M, U)) : (0 : M ⟶ N).app U m = 0 := rfl
findings.problem: These two element-level restatements of `Hom.app` for `0` and `≫` are not simp-tagged and are not used anywhere in the file. Mathlib already has `@[simp] Hom.zero_app` and `@[simp] Hom.comp_app`, which normalise `(0 : M ⟶ N).app U` to `0` and `(φ ≫ ψ).app U` to `φ.app U ≫ ψ.app U`. A hand-written, non-simp copy that sits next to the simp set as a competing normal form leaves two overlapping rewrite interfaces for the same expression. The `(φ ≫ ψ).app U m` lemma also states a different shape (nested application) from Mathlib's simp normal form (composition of maps). So it does not fit the simp set that is actually in use.
findings.proposed_change: Delete `comp_app_apply` and `zero_app_apply`. If an element-level statement is wanted, get it from `simp [Scheme.Modules.Hom.comp_app, Scheme.Modules.Hom.zero_app]` or `ConcreteCategory.comp_apply`. If a local copy stays, name it after Mathlib's lemmas and mark it as an `rfl`-lemma that is meant to be used by `rw`, not by `simp`.
findings.benefit: The file uses the single canonical simp normal form for module-homomorphism application. There are no shadow lemmas that look like part of the simp interface but are never used.

findings.excerpt: theorem pull_sub (V : X.Opens) (m m' : Γ(M, V)) : pull p M V (m - m') = pull p M V m - pull p M V m' := map_sub _ _ _
findings.problem: `pull` is an `abbrev` for `(η p M).app V m`, and each of these lemmas is proved by `map_add _ _ _`, `map_sub _ _ _` or `map_zero _`. They are the generic additive-hom simp lemmas, restated for one abbreviation, and none is simp-tagged. The call sites therefore need a hand-written `rw [pull_add, pull_sub, pull_zero] at key2` (line 166) and `rw [pull_sub, map_sub]` (line 264), which mixes the specific lemma with the generic one. Making them `@[simp]` would add rules that duplicate `map_add`, `map_sub` and `map_zero`. The abbrev unfolds reducibly, so the LHS is not a distinct pattern.
findings.proposed_change: Remove the three lemmas. In `d_u'` and `exists_v`, use `map_add`, `map_sub` and `map_zero` (or `simp only [map_add, map_sub, map_zero]`) directly. This is the same lemma family already used on the next line (`rw [map_add, map_sub, map_zero] at key3`).
findings.benefit: The file has one rewrite vocabulary for additivity. It carries no redundant lemmas that would turn into competing simp rules if someone later added `@[simp]`.

findings.excerpt: simp only [← ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
findings.problem: The same four-lemma `simp only` is repeated at lines 141, 242 and 252. It runs three lemmas in the reverse direction (`← comp_apply`, `← Functor.map_comp`, `← op_comp`), and these turn nested restriction maps into one composite map. Reverse-oriented generic lemmas are fragile and obscure the intent, and each call site is a small hand-built simp set. The file has no canonical lemma saying that two restrictions along `homOfLE` collapse to one. That is why `map_pull`, `F_res_apply` and `res_res` are combined this way at every site. The rewrite is only ever used as a proof-by-closing step and does not describe a forward normal form.
findings.proposed_change: Add one forward lemma for `N.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₂).op (N.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₁).op x) = N.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁.trans h₂)).op x` (once for `X.Modules` and once for the pulled-back module's `presheaf`), proved by the existing simp chain. Use it with `rw` or `simp only` at the three sites. It could also be tagged `@[simp]`, since the RHS has strictly fewer `map` applications and so cannot loop. The proofs would shrink to a call of this lemma, and the proof irrelevance of `≤` proofs makes it hold for any `h₂ ∘ h₁`.
findings.benefit: The three proofs become short and robust. The orientation is the natural forward one (collapsing composites). The reversed-lemma chain is stated once and not copied.
